title: Clear shifts removes only the old lead's whole-work-order shifts
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View, Work orders > Create & Edit and Schedule access, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.
  • Technician {Technician-A} (for example Esther Howard) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on, the Service department, and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Technician {Technician-B} (for example Ralph Edwards) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on, the Service department, and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Technician {Technician-C} (for example Dana Ortiz) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on, the Service department, and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Clear Shifts Scope") is used by this case only.
  • Approved work order {Work-order-1} (for example S10043-17581) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-A} and has two approved lines, {Line-1} (for example "Service - Full grease service") and {Line-2} (for example "Service - Adjust clutch").
  • Approved work order {Work-order-2} (for example S10043-17582) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-A} and has two approved lines, {Line-3} (for example "Service - Full grease service") and {Line-4} (for example "Service - Adjust clutch").
  • Approved work order {Work-order-3} (for example S10043-17583) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-A} and has two approved lines (for example "Service - Full grease service" and "Service - Adjust clutch").
  • {Work-order-1} has three shifts tomorrow: {Technician-A} 8:00–12:00 covering the entire work order, {Technician-A} 13:00–15:00 on {Line-1} only, and {Technician-C} 8:00–10:00 covering the entire work order.
  • {Work-order-2} has two shifts tomorrow: {Technician-A} 8:00–12:00 covering the entire work order, and {Technician-A} 13:00–15:00 on {Line-3} only.
  • {Work-order-3} has one shift the day after tomorrow: {Technician-A} 8:00–12:00 covering the entire work order.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and click Board View in the display switcher.
  2. Type the name of {Customer-A} in Search.
  3. Drag {Work-order-1} from {Technician-A}'s column into {Technician-B}'s column.
  4. Read the question that opens.
  5. Click Clear shifts.
  6. Drag {Work-order-2} from {Technician-A}'s column into {Technician-B}'s column.
  7. In the question that opens, click Keep shifts.
  8. Click Schedule in the top menu.
  9. Use the arrow next to Today to go to tomorrow.
  10. Read every shift on {Work-order-1} and {Work-order-2}.
  11. Use the arrow again to go to the day after tomorrow.
  12. Read the shift on {Work-order-3}.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Steps 4 and 7: both drags open the question "Clear {Technician-A}'s scheduled shifts?" (with the example name: "Clear Esther Howard's scheduled shifts?").
  • Step 5: {Work-order-1} moves to {Technician-B}'s column.
  • Step 10: on {Work-order-1}, {Technician-A}'s 8:00–12:00 shift covering the entire work order is gone, and {Technician-C}'s 8:00–10:00 shift is still there.
  • Step 12: {Technician-A}'s 8:00–12:00 shift on {Work-order-3} is still there, unchanged.
  • Steps 7 and 10: {Work-order-2} is now in {Technician-B}'s column, and both of {Technician-A}'s shifts on it (8:00–12:00 and 13:00–15:00) are still there.
  • Step 10: {Technician-A}'s 13:00–15:00 shifts on {Line-1} of {Work-order-1} and on {Line-3} of {Work-order-2} are still there: the question never clears a shift on only some lines.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 48 (12 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S4-R11, S4-R22, S4-R23, S4-R24, S4-R28 (reworded in version 47 on 12 Oct 2026 after SV-11126: a work-order-level shift is one that covers every current line) and S4-R29, read 14 Oct 2026. Review Decisions DR-31 (optional whole-work-order shift clearing). Schedule shift window labels "Entire work order" / "Choose lines" from the Schedule suite. Each work order has two lines so that the 13:00–15:00 shift covers only some of them; whether a shift on the only line of a one-line work order counts is an open question to the PO (14 Oct 2026). Source-verified 14 October 2026. This version of the case has not yet been checked against a build (the previous version was last checked against build v26.40.8-7a95011 on 10/8/2026).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-R11: “When changing the lead technician in Board View or Tech View, ask whether to clear the outgoing lead’s work-order-level scheduled shifts.”
  • S4-R29: “The prompt reads: title “Clear {Name}'s scheduled shifts?” (with no name: “Clear the lead technician's scheduled shifts?”); text “{Name} has shifts scheduled for this whole work order. Clearing removes shifts that haven't started and ends one that's under way now. Shifts on individual lines and recorded time don't change.”; buttons “Keep shifts”, “Clear shifts” and “Cancel”.”
  • S4-R22: “If the user chooses to clear shifts, remove only the outgoing lead’s shifts scheduled against that whole work order.”
  • S4-R23: “If the user chooses to keep shifts, change the lead technician and retain the existing shifts.”
  • S4-R24: “Never clear shifts scheduled against individual work order lines through this prompt.”
  • S4-R28: “The shift-clearing prompt (S4-R11, S4-R26) shows only when the outgoing lead has a work-order-level shift on this work order that has not ended. A work-order-level shift is one that covers every current line of the work order, which is what the Schedule's Entire work order drop creates. A shift on only some lines does not show the prompt.”

AUTOMATION: READY
